spec_features.spec_quote: Stop at the turn budget or when the give-up sentinel appears.
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:414 `for turn_index in range(turn_budget)` bounds the loop; turn_budget resolved at harness.py:402 from task/config.turn_budgets. harness.py:474-476 sets stop_reason='give_up' when sentinel appears and 'turn_budget' on the last turn; harness.py:493-494 `if stop_reason=='give_up': break`. Both halt paths actually run and end execution.
spec_features.notes: turn_budget is the loop range bound, so it always terminates; give-up causes an explicit break. Both arms of the OR are enforced.

spec_features.spec_quote: A configurable `<<GIVE_UP>>` token; if it appears... the loop stops
spec_features.evidence: config.py:98 `give_up_sentinel: str = "<<GIVE_UP>>"` (configurable). harness.py:403-404 injects it into SYSTEM_PROMPT ('you may emit the token {give_up} on its own line to stop', harness.py:46) so the subject is actually told about the exit. harness.py:474 `if give_up.lower() in assistant_text.lower(): stop_reason='give_up'` then harness.py:493-494 breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: instruction delivered to subject, detection (case-insensitive substring), and honored as a stop via break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # If the subject emits this token (case-insensitive, as a standalone marker) the loop terminates early with stop_reason="give_up". (config.py:96-97, neutral, no welfare language)

spec_features.spec_quote: Giving the model an explicit exit is also the more humane design for welfare-relevant research
